title: Cancer-Myth: Evaluating Large Language Models on Patient Questions with False Presuppositions

live_model.evidence: "responses from frontier LLMs GPT-4-Turbo (OpenAI, 2023), Gemini-1.5-Pro..."; "While GPT-4-Turbo is the best model for providing factual and helpful medical responses (Figure 2)"; Figure 6 (Category-wise Presupposition Correction Score per model, includes GPT-4-Turbo).

prompt.location: Sec 4.2 ("all models are evaluated in a zero-shot setup"); Appendix figures (e.g. Figure 10, 13) show generator/verifier prompts for GPT-4o specifically
prompt.note: Zero-shot protocol is stated; the subject-model query prompt itself (patient question) is the Cancer-Myth item text, but the exact wrapper instruction given to each subject model is not clearly isolated for GPT-4-Turbo in the retrieved text.

claim.metric: Presupposition Correction Rate (PCR), GPT-4-Turbo (value only shown graphically)
claim.location: Figure 5a/Figure 6 (graphical only); text states numeric PCR only for GPT-5 (42.1%), Gemini-2.5-Pro (41.4%), Claude-4-Sonnet (40.0%), Gemini-1.5-Pro (27.2%) and GPT-4o (5.8%) -- GPT-4-Turbo's PCR is not stated as a number in prose

data.source: Cancer-Myth benchmark (patient questions with false presuppositions); paper states dataset construction via GPT-4o + RAG, release status not confirmed in retrieved text

notes: GPT-4-Turbo is tested as a subject model under the same zero-shot protocol as GPT-5/Gemini/Claude, but its headline Presupposition Correction Rate/Score is only shown in bar charts (Figures 2, 5a, 6), never as a table or prose number, so no reproducible target value could be extracted. The paper's judge/verifier throughout is GPT-4o (gpt-4o-2024-05-13), validated against human annotations (Table 2, Appendix C.1.1: 71.1% agreement on the 3-point scale).
